- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias of 3–8% for low sentiment windows.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows after volatility spikes; if forecast shows >10% deviation from 14-day moving average, adjust downward.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 7–10 days of the 30d horizon; apply stronger correction (5–10%) to early days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising from 0.0 to 1.0), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for each 0.1 increase in sentiment trend.
